rv.q: If it doesn't please you, you're too tough to please.
“Wicked” boasts ugly costumes, ugly choreography and an ugly set by Eugene Lee.
With her knockout star turn in "Wicked," Kristin Chenoweth establishes herself as the most bewitching musical-comedy actress of her generation.
She provides the essential helium in a bloated production that might otherwise spend close to three hours flapping its oversized wings without taking off.
A strenuous effort to be all things to all people tends to weigh down this lumbering, overstuffed $14 million production.
One can see where the $14 million went, though one cannot applaud their sense of direction.
Ms. Chenoweth coos and vibrates like Little Lulu, Ms. Menzel even makes green makeup attractive, and they both raise the roof with some of the most sensational singing on Broadway.
A marvel of organization and inventiveness. Lusciously composed, smartly written and beautifully staged, 'Wicked' is one of the rare shows in town that justifies a $100 ticket.
In toto (we couldn’t resist), there are so many wonderful things in Wicked that to dismiss it — as so many critics have done — strikes us as perverse.
Remember the last time an original Broadway musical made you laugh, cry and think — in the right places, and for the right reasons?
Wicked works because it has something Broadway musicals, so addicted to facetiousness and camp, have largely given up on: a story that adults can take seriously.
Everything looks so tangible, touchable, that that in and of itself turns the production into an argument for live theater.
I know I’ve nit-picked, and though there are nits to pick, it’s time for me to say “Wick-KEDDD” in a guttural voice that conveys a good deal of respect.
Its reach, its attempt to be meaty and relevant and theatrical, is not only admirable, it's stimulating.
It's real weak spot is the music which is not helped by Wayne Cliento's standard issue choreography.
What is spectacular about the show is the spectacle.

The problem with the show's book is that it has to cover so much ground in a connect-the-dots fashion that we're deprived of the necessary depth and character development to make us really care about Elphaba or her unlikely friend Galinda.
Nothing about "Wicked" is magical.

Starting November 4, Tuesday at 7 PM. Ticket price: $100, $70, $55, $40 Tickets: Ticketmaster Depicting the façade and inner workings of the Time Dragon Clock, a predictor or perhaps moderator of fate, the cogs and complex weight systems comprising Eugene Lee's set for Wicked , the new musical at the Gershwin, are unavoidably prophetic: this is...
Hence Wicked, a hideous mess of a musical that wants to be many different things, and rarely succeeds in being any of them.
I’m in love with this show; I’m in love with the message it sends and the lesson that there is perhaps wickedness thrust upon good people at times.

This show is amazing and I highly recommend it to anyone who ever loved the Wizard of Oz, who loves broadway, who loves singing and dancing and loves to see a full stage of special effects, detailed costumes and an overall great show.
The latest incarnation of this impeccably oiled entertainment machine finds a new gear courtesy of a British import.
Wicked is simultaneously an entertaining, well crafted, and intelligent show.
It is an incredibly successful merging of dramatic spectacle and character development - and is one of the few truly unforgettable moments I have seen in a Broadway musical.

aw.sub: Won Best Actress in a Musical + 2 more

cn.t: Critics are divided on this lavish spectacle, praising Menzel and Chenoweth's performances and Schwartz's score while faulting its overstuffed plot and uneven tone. Despite mixed reviews, most agree it's an entertaining crowd-pleaser.

sg.ra: Choose Center Orchestra rows F-L for an optimal distance and an unhindered view of the whole stage. These rows sit far enough back to avoid the uncomfortable upward gaze of the front few rows.
The front rows of Center Mezzanine give an elevated view of the whole stage. Choose Row A for the best view at this level and a full-stage perspective.

sg.n: Side Orchestra partially obstructed (above Row G)
sg.ra: Choose marked obstructed-view side-orchestra seats above Row G for decent seats at a decent price. Expect to miss some scenic background rather than much stage action.
Expect the mezzanine overhang to potentially cut off the very top of the stage.

sn.c: Orchestra rows BB-EE force an upward gaze that may become uncomfortable.
sn.sh: Raised stage forces an upward gaze

sn.c: Middle and Rear Mezzanine rows F-N are typically among the cheapest tickets.

sn.lo: Mezzanine, far sides, rows AA to BB
sn.c: Rows AA and BB have just three seats and offer a box-like feel with a side-on view of the stage.
sn.sh: Three seats and a side-on view

sn.lo: Center Orchestra, rows F to L
sn.c: Centre Orchestra rows F to L provide an unhindered view of the whole stage.
sn.sh: Unhindered view of the whole stage

sn.c: Legroom at row F is particularly spacious because there is an aisle where row E would otherwise be.

vs.sum: Broadway's largest theater (1,933 seats) delivers spectacle but the sheer size means rear orchestra and mezzanine seats feel very far from the stage. Sound systems compensate for the distance but intimacy is sacrificed. Legroom is average despite the theater's scale.

acc.note: First Broadway theater with hearing loop (2013). Elevator to Orchestra and Mezzanine. 12 wheelchair spaces.
